ai_show_review.summary: Soaring Dark Star and blistering Eleven dominate a fiery early‑69 set
ai_show_review.blurb: The concert launches with Good Morning Little School Girl before exploding into an extended Dark Star that showcases the band's tight interplay. Highlights include a ferocious The Eleven and a rousing Turn On Your Lovelight powered by Pigpen’s organ and harmonica. Jerry’s guitar is front‑and‑center, driving the improvisations throughout.
ai_show_review.review: On February 2, 1969 at Minneapolis’ Labor Temple the Dead delivered an early‑summer psychedelic surge that still feels electric today. The set opens with a rollicking Good Morning Little School Girl and quickly lifts into a soaring Dark Star where Jerry Garcia’s amp‑driven tone takes command, weaving through tight transitions into Saint Stephen and then a mind‑bending Eleven that crackles with post‑Schoolgirl anger. Pigpen shines on the bluesy turn of The Other One → Cryptical Envelopment and caps the night with a fiery Turn On Your Lovelight, his organ and harmonica adding soulful grit to an already high‑energy arc. Two soundboard sources exist: the Cotsman tape (gd69-02-02.sbd.cotsman.9758.sbeok.shnf) offers an above‑average capture of the entire seven‑song journey despite an uneven, thin low end, while the Miller recording (gd1969-02-02.123283.sbd.miller.flac16) provides a clearer mix but trims some of the flow. Fans seeking the full experience and the iconic Dark Star/Eleven moments will gravitate to the Cotsman version, which the community has flagged as the definitive source.

best_recording.reason: Captures the complete seven‑song arc with soaring Dark Star and blistered Eleven; community consensus marks it as the definitive source despite an uneven mix.

key_highlights: Soaring Dark Star with Jerry’s amp‑driven lead
Blistering The Eleven showcasing aggressive guitar tone
Fiery Turn On Your Lovelight featuring Pigpen’s organ and harmonica
Seamless Other One → Cryptical Envelopment sequence

band_performance.Jerry: Inspired, focused guitar solos dominate the show; his powerful amp‑driven tone drives Dark Star and an aggressive, post‑Schoolgirl anger fuels The Eleven.
